studies.Title: Smoking, alcohol, coffee, tea, caffeine, and theobromine: risk of prostate cancer in Utah (United States).
studies.Reference: Smoking, alcohol, coffee, tea, caffeine, and theobromine: risk of prostate cancer in Utah (United States).
studies.Population: Newly diagnosed prostate cancer cases and age-matched controls in Utah
studies.comparison_type: 11-20 mg/day versus very low theobromine intake among older men, all tumors

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Data from a population-based study of newly diagnosed cases of prostate cancer (n = 362) and age-matched controls (n = 685) conducted in Utah (United States) between 1983 and 1986 were used to determine if cigarette smoking, alcohol, coffee, tea, caffeine, and theobromine were associated with prostate cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: Data from a population-based study of newly diagnosed cases of prostate cancer (n = 362) and age-matched controls (n = 685) conducted in Utah (United States) between 1983 and 1986 were used to determine if cigarette smoking, alcohol, coffee, tea, caffeine, and theobromine were associated with prostate cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Compared with men with very low levels of theobromine intake, older men consuming 11 to 20 and over 20 mg of theobromine per day were at increased risk of prostate cancer (odds ratio [OR] for all tumors = 2.06, 95 percent confidence interval [CI] = 1.33-3.20, and OR = 1.47, CI = 0.99-2.19, respectively; OR for aggressive tumors = 1.90, CI = 0.90-3.97, and OR = 1.74, CI = 0.91-3.32, respectively).
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: Compared with men with very low levels of theobromine intake, older men consuming 11 to 20 and over 20 mg of theobromine per day were at increased risk of prostate cancer (odds ratio [OR] for all tumors = 2.06, 95 percent confidence interval [CI] = 1.33-3.20, and OR = 1.47, CI = 0.99-2.19, respectively; OR for aggressive tumors = 1.90, CI = 0.90-3.97, and OR = 1.74, CI = 0.91-3.32, respectively).
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: Compared with men with very low levels of theobromine intake, older men consuming 11 to 20 and over 20 mg of theobromine per day
extraction_supporting_text.design: Data from a population-based study of newly diagnosed cases of prostate cancer
extraction_supporting_text.timing: conducted in Utah (United States) between 1983 and 1986
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: older men consuming 11 to 20 and over 20 mg of theobromine per day
